answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils through trust-graph routing across a network atlas. The protocol tracks bounded random walks from seed nodes at an ingress jetty to score candidate peers. Because graph bottlenecks prevent trust flow into synthetic clusters, an attacker must secure scarce, authentic endorsement edges from honest nodes per identity. However, this creates cold-start penalties for an honest sparrow agent lacking prior connections, and fails if primary seeds are compromised.
